channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Financial Times] Republicans choose Jim Jordan as House minority leader
item.description: Pugnacious lawmaker signals uncompromising stance despite party’s poor US midterms performance

item.title: [Politico Europe] Nvidia hires Wachtell Lipton for Jensen Huang investigation
item.description: The independent investigation follows reports that the CEO had a romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Poland says Pentagon backs permanent US base, with Trump decision due in December
item.description: Warsaw is seeking a lasting American military commitment as NATO allies fear further U.S. troop withdrawals from Europe.

item.title: [Financial Times] US commerce department delays Megaspeed’s inclusion on trade blacklist
item.description: Company connected to alleged Chinese spy who had affair with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was left off ‘entity list’

item.title: [Financial Times] US regulator postpones Wall Street push to trade AI computing futures
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission raises concerns over price manipulation as exchanges race to create new asset class

item.title: [Financial Times] Senior US soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: British Counter Terrorism Policing’s investigation involves the FBI and American military

item.title: [Politico Europe] Brussels takes on the evils of online commerce
item.description: The EU is proposing new rules that would fine companies that use manipulative online tactics like "dynamic pricing" and "addictive design" to lure consumers to buy and pay more.

item.title: [DW] British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
item.description: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine and Russia discuss prisoner swap deal during ‘constructive’ talks
item.description: Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed a positive day of direct negotiations with Russia in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia hires former US prosecutor at Wachtell to lead Jensen Huang probe
item.description: Former acting head of US attorney’s office for Southern District of New York tapped for investigation of CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy

item.title: [DW] UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
item.description: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

item.title: [EU Observer] Best way to halt migration is to sabotage Europe’s economy – but nobody wants that, so what are the alternatives?
item.description: Keeping people impoverished abroad and destroying its economy are Europe's best tools to stop migration. Not even the most anti-migrant politician would seriously push for such a proposal.

item.title: [Financial Times] Treasuries slide as ‘hot’ inflation sparks bets on Fed rate rise
item.description: Two-year government bond yields soar most since 2024 as October consumer price growth tops forecasts

item.title: [Euractiv] EU official rejects anonymous corruption allegations
item.description: Isabelle Le Galo Flores firmly denies any wrongdoing

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine : Mélenchon embarrassé
item.description: Voilà trois jours que Jean-Luc Mélenchon vitupère contre ses adversaires, le gouvernement, et les médias, qui caricaturent, d’après lui, ses propositions pour mettre fin à la guerre en Ukraine. Le candidat Insoumis cherche à s’extirper des accusations formulées contre lui selon lesquelles il s’alignerait en partie sur les positions de Moscou. Pourquoi cette réaction épidermique […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Portugal slams Rutte for ‘regrettable’ claim that Lisbon downplays Russian threat
item.description: Portugal’s foreign ministry on Tuesday slammed Mark Rutte after the NATO chief said that for Lisbon, Russia was a distant and less relevant threat. “Portugal, its Government and its people have never been in any doubt about which side of history they stand on,” the ministry said on X. “It is regrettable that the NATO […]

item.title: [DW] Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
item.description: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

item.title: [Politico Europe] L’Europe a besoin de Nvidia et il faudra plus qu’un scandale d’espionnage pour que ça change
item.description: Jensen Huang, le PDG du fabricant américain de puces, a peut-être était la cible d’une opération d’espionnage chinoise. Même si c’était avéré, il n’existe aucune alternative européenne à Nvidia.

item.title: [Euractiv] Military mobility solidarity pool to be set up in a year, new draft says
item.description: Military mobility solidarity pool to be set up within a year, new draft shows

item.title: [Politico Europe] 5 ways Spain’s conservatives plan to put the country on a new course
item.description: The People's Party launched its manifesto on Tuesday.

item.title: [EU Observer] Watchdog finds patchy customs controls leave big loopholes in EU’s Russia trade sanctions
item.description: Watchdog finds spotty oversight and unclear rules weaken EU trade sanctions with Russia. Calls on customs authorities and the European Commission to do a better job.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Countries on the fence over COP31’s flagship target
item.description: Electrification pledge only has a handful of explicit endorsements so far.

item.title: [Euractiv] The trilateral no one’s talking about
item.description: Also, in tonight’s edition: EU and US close ranks behind NATO ahead of Abu Dhabi

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] From aid donor to ‘geopolitical actor’: EU’s Africa diplomat on upgrading security cooperation
item.description: The EU is advancing its role as a 'geopolitical actor' by accelerating defence and security talks with a series of African states. EUobserver talks to Patricia Llombart Cussac, the managing director for Africa for the European External Action Service, the EU’s diplomatic corps.

item.title: [Euractiv] EXCLUSIVE: EU socialists push common defence, double down on Kyiv
item.description: Socialist group set to adopt ambitious new defence position paper

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Made in Europe’ and low-carbon rules up for debate as EU eyes industrial law deal
item.description: EU deputy ambassadors meet on Wednesday to settle which countries count as 'European' and what may count as 'low carbon', as the Irish EU presidency races to strike a deal among member states before the end of the year.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Surge in EV demand blows past German government’s subsidy forecasts
item.description: The government expected its EV subsidy scheme to run through 2029 — it may be out of cash by the end of next year.

item.title: [Euractiv] Italy’s F-35 bill jumps by €7 billion
item.description: The ministry attributes the higher bill to 'rising costs of technological upgrades and the euro-dollar exchange rate'

item.title: [Financial Times] Alice Huang’s tangled web of connections
item.description: Executive alleged to be Chinese spy who had affair with Nvidia chief had already built career alongside a man with a history of crossing regulators

item.title: [Euractiv] EU watchdog to inspect Commission documents in AI envoy probe
item.description: Ombudsman inquiry adds to troubles for von der Leyen’s AI pick

item.title: [Financial Times] Top Fed official considers largest rate rise since 2022
item.description: Governor Christopher Waller says policymakers should weigh a 50bp move if US inflation fails to slow

item.title: [Euractiv] EU auditors: Russia sanctions undermined by ‘weak’ enforcement
item.description: So-called ‘forum-shopping’ is harming Europe's ability to ramp up pressure on Moscow

item.title: [DW] Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
item.description: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

item.title: [Financial Times] US, Russia and Ukraine resume talks on ending war
item.description: Expectations of a breakthrough are low because Vladimir Putin shows no sign of wanting to halt the conflict

item.title: [Euractiv] Spanish opposition vows to join EU’s migration hardline
item.description: The conservative People’s Party (PP) unveils its manifesto ahead of elections this month

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs agree sovereign rules for picking satellite-to-phone operators
item.description: Tentative shadow rapporteurs' deal has backing from EPP, S&D and Renew

item.title: [EU Observer] Digital Fairness Act: EU cracks down on influencer ads and manipulative app design
item.description: The Digital Fairness Act aims to impose stricter protections for people online. While the leaked draft proposes to ban overly-complicated choices to refuse data-sharing, it does not ban addictive design practises outright, warns rights watchdog EDRi. Meanwhile, online retailer Omio have complained that compliance will be costly to businesses.

item.title: [Euractiv] Turkish electrification pledge gains little traction at COP31
item.description: Australia, leading negotiations in Antalya, concedes 35% target is 'a challenge'

item.title: [Euractiv] German-Ukrainian duo elected to lead new EU-Ukraine drone alliance
item.description: Quantum Systems teamed up with UFORCE to secure the first term as co-chair

item.title: [Euractiv] Climate action and health resilience are ‘investments in the same thing’, experts say [Partner Content]
item.description: Health systems must protect patients from climate impacts while cutting their own emissions. Experts at the World Health Summit in Berlin said the two tasks reinforce each other, and that prevention serves both.

item.title: [EU Observer] As many Russians killed near Pokrovsk in Ukraine as Soviet troops killed in the 1945 Battle of Berlin, according to hacked data (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,720)
item.description: The data leak reveals a war so costly that battles around Pokrovsk now rival some of the most arrowing clashes of WW2, potentially reshaping how Moscow and Kyiv — as well as their allies — calculate their next moves on the front.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Commission to host security talks after week of bomb hoaxes that hit 20 airports and dozens of European flights
item.description: Experts from EU member states will meet on Wednesday to discuss last week’s bomb hoaxes affecting dozens of flights across Europe and causing millions in losses.

item.title: [EU Observer] The Kraków shooting: A Polish tragedy, a Russian opportunity
item.description: As soon as a few images of the perpetrator and the contents of the boot of his car appeared in the media, the Russian propaganda machine was set to work.

item.title: [Euractiv] Merz and Magyar clash over Ukraine and EU budget
item.description: German chancellor and Hungarian PM are at odds over including support for Kyiv in EU budget

item.title: [Euractiv] EU farmers to stage rally during Dublin summit
item.description: Talks are already under way for a large protest during the next European Council meeting in Brussels

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Italy’s Meloni is EU’s best hope of charming Putin at Ukraine peace talks, former Russian spy says
item.description: Any EU envoy for peace talks with Russia should meet four criteria, the Russian ex-spy said: no border with Russia, no conflicts of interest, no fear of Donald Trump, and willingness to "bloody" Vladimir Putin's nose.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU-backed Black Sea security hub to become operational in 2027
item.description: Bucharest and Sofia are negotiating a memorandum of understanding to operationalise the Hub

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4tn in IPO
item.description: The Claude maker plans to raise as much as $64bn in highly anticipated listing

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
item.description: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump is taking the Alamo route
item.description: Accepting defeat with grace would go against a lifetime of going for broke

item.title: [EU Observer] EU anger as Malta vetoes €13bn EU‑wide tobacco tax overhaul
item.description: Maltese finance minister Clyde Caruana said Malta "supports the objectives" of the reform, but said that the "proposed minimum [excise tax] rates remain well above current national levels."

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
item.description: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What can we expect from Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi?
item.description: Talks on peace in Ukraine are set to continue this week in Abu Dhabi. And this time, the EU appears to have found a way into the room. But what can actually be expected from these negotiations?

item.title: [DW] US, Russia and Ukraine start talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US are getting underway in the United Arab Emirates. It is the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Investigation] Thousands deported with Frontex help never see promised EU reintegration money
item.description: Internal minutes show Frontex urging national authorities and NGOs to run sensitive data past the agency before talking to journalists, even as it insists “transparency is the rule” and refuses to release basic figures on who actually got paid.

item.title: [Financial Times] VW pivots again as ‘In China, For China’ runs out of road
item.description: The German group is changing its strategy in the world’s largest car market as it struggles with a sharp downturn

item.title: [DW] Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
item.description: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

item.title: [DW] Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
item.description: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

item.title: [DW] Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
item.description: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
item.description: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: [DW] New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
item.description: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

item.title: [DW] Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
item.description: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

item.title: [DW] EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
item.description: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.

item.title: [DW] Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
item.description: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.

item.title: [EU Observer] €120m in totally unused border facilities is the latest bill for the monumental waste that was Brexit
item.description: Hundreds of millions have been wasted on Brexit border checks that either don't work or were never used. It's a fitting monument to a failure to plan.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs demand Belgium evacuate visa-holders from Gaza as winter flooding makes life catastrophic
item.description: 1,800 people hold Belgian visas for family reunifications or university studies, yet remain stuck in Gaza. And while EU officials and Belgian authorities pass accountability back and forth, devastating floods have displaced even more already displaced people - and a handful of MEPs stand up for the Palestinians that will have to suffer another winter outdoors.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia goes quiet on claims of territorial wins, starts bragging about air-strikes on Ukrainian cities instead (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,719)
item.description: Russian Z-channels have stopped reporting on movements along the contact lines, instead publishing lists of cities struck by Russian drones and missiles.
